Triage: lands in `scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs` plus the two registry entries it names → `domain:devx` (shared gate, general test-resolution tooling); queued `pm:queue`.

Route suggestion (input, not a ruling): option A — teach `asPath` the template-literal form — is the contract-first shape: the configs are correct, the reader is what cannot see them, and B would penalise the one-rule-for-all-namespaces form both configs deliberately use. Shrink the two registry entries (`plugin-audit`, `service-knowledge` → exactly `["@objectstack/objectql"]`) in the same PR, since the gate audits both directions and will name them.

Priority: normal — the gate is fail-closed today, so the cost is over-stated remediation work and a misleading failure text, not a false green.

Sibling card #8024 claimed the same round is `scripts/check-skill-frame-freshness.mjs` — different file.

**This is a defect in what this seat shipped ~4 hours ago** (PR #7966, card #7849). Following it through is this seat's responsibility, not a new lane's.

**Premise verified on `origin/main`, exactly as filed:**

| package | alias line | in registry as unaliased? |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/plugin-audit` | `vitest.config.ts:39` — ``replacement: `${path.resolve(__dirname, '../../spec/src')}/$1/index.ts` `` | **yes** (wrongly) |
| `@objectstack/service-knowledge` | `vitest.config.ts:23` — same template-literal form | **yes** (wrongly) |

Those are the only two files in the repo using the template-literal replacement form, and both are recorded as still resolving spec through `dist/`. They do not.

## ⭐ These two packages are the repo's alias-parsing canary — twice over

The same two packages defeated **my own census** this morning, by a *different* mechanism: I grepped `objectstack/core` and missed them because the anchored-regex form writes the bytes `objectstack\/core` with an **escaped slash**. Now the shipped gate misses them because their spec-subpath alias uses a **template-literal replacement**.

Two independent readers, two different parsing assumptions, **the same two packages wrong both times**. They are the ones whose alias spellings are unusual enough to break naive readers, which makes them the natural fixture for any tool that reads vitest aliases. Carried into the dispatch as a required test case rather than a nice-to-have.

## Registry before/after — the full delta

Measured with `--list` on both sides of the change. `diff` reports exactly two rows; every other line is byte-identical.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `@objectstack/plugin-audit` | `['@objectstack/objectql', '@objectstack/spec']` | `['@objectstack/objectql']` |
| `@objectstack/service-knowledge` | `['@objectstack/objectql', '@objectstack/spec']` | `['@objectstack/objectql']` |
| registry entries | 63 | 63 — unchanged; both packages keep `objectql`, so neither entry is deleted |
| package-dependency pairs | 312 | 310 |

**No package was reclassified that nobody suspected.** The dispatch flagged that a reader newly parsing a form might surface more — it did not: the template-literal replacement appears in exactly two files repo-wide (10 of the 12 replacements in 15 alias-bearing configs are plain `path.resolve(…)` calls; zero use `+`), so the blast radius is the two entries predicted and nothing else.

## Block 3 — evaluate the config, or keep parsing source text?

Measured before choosing, and the answer was decisive: **stay with source-text parsing.** There is no `node_modules` in this repo as the gate reaches it — `ls node_modules` fails at the repo root and in the worktree — and the gate runs dependency-free in ~3.0s, with a self-test that builds its fixture tree in `tmpdir` with none either. Every real config here opens with `import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'`, so evaluation would trade a bare-checkout gate for one that cannot run before `pnpm install`, and would turn an alias list the gate merely *reads* into one it *executes*. Recorded in the `asPath` header so it is not re-litigated.

Legal spellings that remain unreadable, all fail-closed, enumerated in that header: `+` concatenation; a hole or argument with no string literal (`${SPEC_SRC}`, `path.resolve(SRC_ROOT, 'index.ts')`); a path that is not the last argument; a template nested inside a `${…}` hole. The `+` form is the same defect one spelling over and is filed as #8108 rather than fixed here.

## Reverse verification — direction predicted first, then measured

**Predicted:** removing the reader's new template branch while the registry stays shrunk flips the failure to the **`added` direction, not `STALE`** — the subpath aliases go invisible again, so `@objectstack/spec` re-enters the measurement while the registry no longer lists it.

**Observed, matching:**

```
  x @objectstack/plugin-audit: NEW unaliased artifact import(s) since this entry was measured: @objectstack/spec.
  x @objectstack/service-knowledge: NEW unaliased artifact import(s) since this entry was measured: @objectstack/spec.
```

The self-test went red on exactly the three predicted assertions — canary reported, the `${…}` hole not failing as unreadable, the canary's both-directions audit — while the `dist/` and ENOTDIR template fixtures stayed green, which was also predicted: the old reader happens to answer those two correctly, so they do not discriminate. Fix restored from the commit; tree clean.

**ACCEPT** — PR #8107. Reviewed against GitHub, not the report's self-description.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| path surface (`get_files`) | **1 file** — `scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs`. **Zero `packages/**/vitest.config.ts`** ⇒ ruling 3 honoured; the configs were right and stayed untouched |
| registry delta | **exactly two entries narrowed**, not removed: `plugin-audit` and `service-knowledge` each drop `@objectstack/spec` and keep `@objectstack/objectql`. Precise — those packages alias spec but genuinely still resolve objectql through `dist/` |
| CI | **23 checks, zero failures** |

Both halves landed together per ruling 1: the reader learns the form, then the registry shrinks to match. Neither an allowlist nor a config rewrite — the two shapes ruling 2 and 3 forbade.

## It rejected config evaluation with a measurement, which is what Block 3 asked for

I flagged "should the reader **evaluate** the config rather than pattern-match its source?" as possibly the real fix and possibly too heavy. Measured answer:

> this gate runs on a bare checkout with **NO `node_modules`** (that is how CI reaches it, and how its own `--self-test` fixture tree in `tmpdir` works), while every real config opens with `import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'`. Evaluation would trade a dependency-free ~3s scan for one that cannot run before `pnpm install`, and would make an alias list the gate cannot see today into one it **executes**.

A constraint I did not know about, decisive, and it also names the security-shaped reason. Settled.

## ⭐ It built the canary I asked for, and made it sharper than the ask

Fixture **(7)** is a byte-for-byte copy of the real shape, pinning **both** spellings that have now defeated readers of these configs — escaped-slash regex `find` *and* template-literal `replacement` — with the reasoning recorded in place:

> Those two packages have now defeated THREE readers of vitest aliases, twice on the same morning, by two different parsing assumptions … Neither spelling is exotic and neither is going away — the escaped slash is forced by the regex literal, the template by the capture group.

It also added the three fixtures that stop "read a template" degrading into "wave a template past": **(8)** a template landing on `dist/` is still unaliased; **(9)** the ENOTDIR prefix trap is still seen *through* a template (proving the chunks are really joined); **(10)** a `${…}` hole with nothing literal in it is **UNREADABLE, not empty** — the fail-closed half. Plus the both-directions audit on the canary, so a now-readable package registered by mistake names itself for deletion.

And it **documented the spellings that remain unreadable** — `+` concatenation (*"the exact #8020 shape one spelling over"*), non-literal holes, a path that is not the last argument, a nested template — each stated as fail-closed, *"listed so the next one is looked up rather than rediscovered"*. That converts an unknown into a known limit, which is the whole difference between a gate you can trust and one you merely hope about.

## Note on what this defect cost, since this seat shipped it

Worth recording plainly: `check:test-source-alias` shipped ~4 hours ago in PR #7966 and was **fail-closed throughout** — it never green-lit a stale-dist package. What it did was **over-state the remediation list and tell two compliant packages to add an alias they already had**. Real, worth fixing same-day, and materially less bad than the failure mode the gate exists to prevent. `#7849 remains open` as the `tracking` anchor for the remaining remediation surface, which is now two entries smaller and more accurate.

Marking ready and arming auto-merge. Tracked to MERGED with the `closed_by_pull_requests` check.
